summary: Iteration 32 — Phase 1 'Efficacité serveur'. Backend: new pytest file test_iter32_sync_ratelimit.py 8/8 pass (after fixing a bug in my own WS test). /sync works: it returns the full data on an empty or old h, the tiny {h,online,waiting} when nothing changed, a new h plus data after a friend request and after POST /solo (current_game.game_id), and 401 with no auth. /sync counts as the presence heartbeat. The legacy endpoints /notifications, /presence/ping, /presence/pulse and /games/current still return 200 with their original shapes. Rate limit: a 100-request burst gave exactly 80x200 + 20x429 {detail:'too_many_requests'}. A second account was not affected, the first account worked again after 10s, and the 429 carries CORS headers. WS dedupe: the first state arrives on connect, bids and plays come through as updates, and a played card leaves the hand. Admin stats returns 200 and shows 'sync (regroupé)' after the metrics flush. Full regression suite: 158 passed, 2 failed. Both failures are flaky and passed when re-run alone: test_ws_game (WS 'no close frame' under load) and test_capot_broken_ends_hand_immediately (depends on the deal; hand_scores [0,520] includes a +20 belote bonus, so the strict 'assert 500 in hand_scores' fails sometimes). Frontend (844x390 landscape): tester1 logs in, Home loads with no console errors, the badge (3) and the friend-request list appear, 'Partie en cours' resume shows and the online count shows. Over ~21s on Home there were exactly 3 /sync calls (~7.1s apart) and zero calls to legacy endpoints. Simulated background (document hidden) for 16s: 0 requests. On resume: an immediate /sync. Matchmaking: /matchmaking/status every ~1.55s for the first 20s, then every 5s; cancel calls DELETE /matchmaking/leave and returns Home.

minor.issue: A 'nothing new' reply only saves bandwidth. Every call still runs the full payload: last_active update, a users count_documents on last_active (that field has no index, so it scans the collection), a scan of mm_queue, the notifications queries (with an N+1 get_room per invite) and the live_games query. At 7s per online user, DB load is roughly the same as before.

The counter is in memory and per process. With several workers or pods the real limit becomes 80 x N per process. It also only applies once the token is cached in _token_users (the first request after a restart is never limited). Acceptable for the current single worker.

action_items: Optional: add an index on users.last_active (the online count runs on every /sync call).
Optional: make the 'nothing new' path cheaper on the server (e.g. cache the digest per user, or skip the notifications and current_game queries when nothing relevant changed).
Optional: loosen test_improvement_pack.py::test_capot_broken_ends_hand_immediately so it accepts 500 plus a belote bonus (e.g. max(hand_scores) >= 500).
critical_code_review_comments: NotificationsContext: the poll loop is correct. pollingRef prevents overlapping polls, the timer is cleared in the background and resumes on 'active', setSlowMode reschedules, and refresh() forces a full payload by clearing h.
game_runtime.broadcast dedupe only skips when there are no events AND the hash matches the last state sent on that socket. No missed updates were seen.
The 429 response from the outer middleware still includes Access-Control-Allow-Origin, so the web client sees a real 429.

success_rate.backend: 100% of new tests (8/8); full suite 158/160 (2 flaky, pass when re-run)
